title: Noah Kahan’s Hilarious PSA After a Concertgoer Leaves a Nasty Surprise
summary:
It was a night to remember at Citizens Bank Park in Philadelphia—but for all the wrong reasons. During Noah Kahan’s Great Divide Tour stop on Friday, someone left a pile of poop on the floor by the seats. A fan-filmed clip of the mess quickly went viral, and the internet did what it does best: erupted in a mix of disgust and dark humor.

Kahan himself jumped into the fray with a post on X that was both a public service announcement and a bizarrely honest confession. “If you have to poop at a show please dear god just go to the bathroom,” he wrote. Then came the twist: “I’ve pooped my pants as much as the next 29 year old but you guys gotta understand there’s a venue worker out there with a 1000 yard stare after dealing with that.”

Yes, the chart-topping singer-songwriter behind The Great Divide admitted to a history of, well, digestive mishaps. In a follow-up comment, he clarified: “I s— myself onstage in Charlottesville but that’s because I am dedicated to my craft.” The juxtaposition of artistic integrity and bathroom emergencies was peak Kahan—self-effacing, absurd, and oddly endearing.

A user with the handle Turd Furguson (you can’t make this up) called him out: “‘As much as the next 29 year old,’ should equate to f—ing ZERO, what the hell are you talking about??” Kahan’s reply? “Okay Turd Ferguson,” keeping the tone lighthearted.

The incident fits into a bizarre trend in live music. Just days earlier, Olivia Rodrigo mentioned smelling diapers from fans in the front row. Whether it’s a lack of facilities or a strange concert culture, Kahan’s message is clear: please, for the love of all that is holy, use the bathroom. His tour continues through December, and one can only hope the next venues are poop-free zones.
why_it_matters: This incident highlights the sometimes wild behavior at live events and how social media allows artists to directly address fans, turning a gross moment into a conversation about concert etiquette and shared public spaces that teens frequent.

background_read: Noah Kahan, an American singer-songwriter from Vermont, rose to mainstream fame with his 2022 album 'Stick Season' and the hit single 'Dial Drunk,' blending folk, pop, and indie rock.
His current 'Great Divide Tour' travels across North America, with the Philadelphia stop at Citizens Bank Park—the 43,000-seat home of the Philadelphia Phillies baseball team.

Bizarre concert behavior has made headlines recently, such as fans throwing objects at artists like Harry Styles and Bebe Rexha, or, as Olivia Rodrigo noted, fans wearing diapers to avoid missing any of the show.
Live music events often become cultural flashpoints, and social media amplifies odd moments, turning even a messy situation into a viral conversation within hours.
Kahan's self-deprecating humor aligns with a broader trend of artists using social media to address fan behavior, creating a more direct and often humorous dialogue with their audience.

perspectives.description: Fans find Kahan’s honesty and humor refreshing, as it makes the artist feel relatable and approachable, strengthening the bond between him and his audience.

Venue staff and many concertgoers worry that such behavior shows a lack of respect for public spaces and the workers who clean up, potentially spoiling the experience for others and creating extra work.

Sociologists might see this as an example of how digital culture amplifies norm-breaking acts, encouraging both shame and entertainment, while raising questions about crowd management and festival hygiene practices.

The incident could push venues to improve facilities and enforce clearer rules of conduct, while artists might encourage more respectful fan behavior through public messages, leading to a cleaner and more enjoyable concert environment for everyone.
